question: A researcher has one research idea and wants to bounce from it to adjacent, exploitable ideas: what methods exist (LLM ideation, literature-based discovery, analogy mining, facet recombination) and how well do they work?

S1.title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?

S3.title: HindSight: Evaluating Research Idea Generation via Future Impact

S5.title: Scideator: Human-LLM Scientific Idea Generation Grounded in Research-Paper Facet Recombination

S6.title: IdeaSynth: Iterative Research Idea Development Through Evolving and Composing Idea Facets with Literature-Grounded Feedback

S7.title: All That Glitters is Not Novel: Plagiarism in AI Generated Research

S8.title: Literature-Grounded Novelty Assessment of Scientific Ideas (Idea Novelty Checker)

S10.title: Unsupervised word embeddings capture latent knowledge from materials science literature

S11.title: Literature-based discovery: addressing the issue of the subpar evaluation methodology

S12.title: ResearchAgent (iterative research idea generation over scientific literature with LLMs)

S15.title: Spark: a system for scientifically creative idea generation

S16.title: GYWI: co-author graphs with retrieval-augmented generation for scientific idea generation

claims.text: In the largest expert study, over 100 NLP researchers judged LLM-generated ideas more novel than human ideas (p < 0.05) and slightly weaker on feasibility.

In the execution study, 43 experts spent over 100 hours each executing assigned ideas; scores of LLM ideas dropped significantly more than those of human ideas (p < 0.05), with rankings flipping on many metrics.
In a time-split test a retrieval-augmented system received 2.5 times higher scores (p < 0.001) while an LLM judge saw no difference (p = 0.584).
Planned retrieval gave 3.4 times more unique novel ideas and at least 2.5 times more top-rated ideas over 170 seed papers in a Swiss Tournament evaluation.
Facet recombination improved human exploration in a user study of 19 participants.
Structured refinement of idea facets improved human exploration in a user study of 20 participants.
24 % of 50 LLM-generated research documents were judged by 13 experts to be paraphrased or significantly borrowed from existing work, and automated plagiarism detectors missed them.
A retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker raised agreement with expert labels by about 13 %.
Analogy mining beat information-retrieval baselines and increased creative idea generation in an experiment.
Word embeddings trained on materials-science literature recommended materials for functional applications several years before their discovery.
A 2023 critique argues that literature-based discovery evaluation has relied on Swanson's two discoveries for 30 years.
Nova, on 170 seed papers in a Swiss Tournament evaluation, reports 3.4 times more unique novel ideas and at least 2.5 times more top-rated ideas; the abstract does not say who the judges were.
Chain of Ideas costs about $0.50 per idea and, per its abstract, outperforms other methods and is comparable to humans, with no sample size stated.
In a within-subjects study with 19 computer-science researchers, Scideator users identified significantly more interesting ideas than with a search-plus-LLM baseline, no effect size in the abstract.

In a lab study with 20 participants, IdeaSynth users explored more alternative ideas and expanded their initial ideas with more detail than with a strong LLM baseline; a deployment study had 7 participants.
The AI Scientist-v2 submitted three fully autonomous manuscripts to an ICLR workshop and one exceeded the average human acceptance threshold.
The end-to-end AI Scientist costs under $15 per paper across three ML subfields and was scored by an automated reviewer described as near-human.
Blind review by over 100 NLP researchers found LLM ideas more novel (p < 0.05) and slightly weaker on feasibility, with failures of LLM self-evaluation and lack of diversity.
43 experts carried out randomly assigned ideas over 100 hours each; after execution LLM idea scores dropped significantly more than human ones (p < 0.05) and rankings flipped on many metrics.
Ideation Arena collected over 6,000 pairwise comparisons from 105 researchers over 14 LLMs and 5 agent frameworks; the best LLM judge reaches 72.56 % soft accuracy against expert preferences.

A study of 912 AI-generated and 41 human economics papers found an idea-quality gap of d = 2.23 and an execution gap of d = 0.90, idea quality accounting for about 71 % of the difference, judged by models.
Station rediscovers 62.7 % of the original findings of three ICLR oral papers, against 15.4 % for a Codex multi-agent baseline and 14.4 to 20.6 % for AI Scientist-v2.
Execution-grounded evolutionary search reached 69.4 % against 48.0 % for a GRPO baseline, and reinforcement learning on execution reward suffered mode collapse.

HindSight, over 10 AI/ML topics and 30 months after a cutoff, gave retrieval-augmented generation 2.5 times higher scores (p < 0.001) while an LLM judge found no difference (p = 0.584); HindSight scores correlated negatively with LLM-judged novelty (rho = -0.29).
Across six judges, small prompt changes shifted pairwise accuracy by over 50 points, and retrieval and larger reasoning budgets helped little.
RINoBench gathers 1,381 expert-judged research ideas; LLM novelty judgments diverge significantly from the human gold standard, including for reasoning models.
Swapping the judge on 4,000 Chatbot Arena battles gave a median Cohen's kappa of 0.22.
Judge flip rates were roughly 5 % on average and about 40 % on close calls across 4 judges and 3 benchmarks.
Thirteen experts judged 50 LLM-generated research documents and found 24 % paraphrased or significantly borrowed from existing work, confirmed by source authors; plagiarism detectors missed them.

In a budgeted-refinement study over 10 random seeds and 10 ideation environments, raw generation and reranking yielded no research-strong nonduplicate ideas, and MMR-k refinement gave the lowest duplicate rate (proxy ratings).
CrossTrace's human check of 150 stratified records found a 0.0 % fabrication rate in its reasoning traces.
An inspiration-retrieval method improves HitRate@top4% by more than 10 percentage points over MOOSE-Chem on ResearchBench.
A retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker with expert-labelled examples reaches about 13 % higher agreement than existing approaches; the facet-based re-ranker ablation matters.

In a design experiment with 32 undergraduate students and three expert raters, AI support was higher on problem framing and mechanism while human-only work was higher on innovation and solution strategy.
Context-based ABC raised B-entity precision from 27.1 % and 22.1 % (co-occurrence) to 71.4 % and 77.9 % (context-based), and to 89 % and 97.5 % with context assignment, on two relations.
A 2021 case study of eight neurodegenerative-disease discoveries shows the limits of the ABC model in open-ended settings and proposes a contrastive approach.

AGATHA used a temporal holdout predicting connections first introduced after 2015 across the twenty most popular relationship types, reporting best-in-class performance without numbers in the abstract.
A retrieval-augmented LLM evaluating A-B-C hypotheses reached Cohen's kappa of 0.84 with four experts on 14 hypotheses; it scores hypotheses and does not generate them.

Analogy mining vectors gave higher precision and recall than information-retrieval baselines, and retrieved analogies significantly increased the likelihood of creative ideas in an ideation experiment (products and patents, no sample size in the abstract).
A cross-pollination retrieval benchmark of 1,300 queries in 26 fields shows the best of 11 retrievers at Recall@10 of 0.26, an LLM reranker at 0.81 and fine-tuning up to 0.70.
A design-ideation experiment found a significant effect of conceptual-similarity inspiration images on novelty, variety and quantity of ideas against random images, sample not stated.
CHIMERA provides a knowledge base of over 28,000 recombination examples from which a model predicts directions researchers find inspiring, with no figure in the abstract.

conclusion: Seed-based LLM ideation is supported on novelty and interaction at small scale (19 to 20 participants) but weak on execution, LLM judges are unreliable, and older literature-based discovery and analogy lines have thinner controlled evidence; the search stopped at its 60-call ceiling.
